text: Make the strongest supportable idea the dominant native text. Choose line breaks, scale and surrounding space from the actual words and brand typography. Support … must not compete with the headline.

When the request leaves imagery optional, a typography-only result is complete … Do not fill quiet space with a generated metaphor, fake metric, pill, card or mandatory CTA … Use the authentic logo if available; never typeset a replacement wordmark.

When the request asks for new imagery, keep type as the dominant message and generate the requested artwork as an independent layer … A flat palette match does not preserve an observed textured, blurred or tonal treatment. Reserve readable space within that treatment rather than deleting it.

In the direction record, name the message, why type carries it, the native text layers and the intended reading order. At feed scale verify immediate comprehension, distinct brand character and readable support.

Name one audience, situation, friction and supported capability. Distinguish an observed pain from a plausible scenario … Keep metrics, universal outcomes and customer claims out without matching evidence. Questions … cannot smuggle in an unsubstantiated accusation.

Inspect relevant company ads and campaign sources before choosing voice or art … Record the visible hierarchy, logo treatment, imagery, copy density and whether the action is in artwork or channel UI … If references are absent, state that gap and derive a direction from the kit without claiming fidelity.

Three compositions: The interruption; The resolved moment; The bottleneck. Alternatives, not required panels. Do not default to a red unhappy half and a green happy half. Choose the image treatment from inspected sources, including their actual texture, lighting and spatial behavior.

Choose the CTA from the available next step and observed campaign behavior … Check: can a viewer explain both the problem and why this product helps? … If the capability link is missing, switch to supported positioning and record the gap.
Ground factual steps in the supplied product/source context. Never invent elapsed time, savings, integrations or a competitor's failures. An illustrative workflow must be described as illustrative.

Choose a spatial relationship: sequence, convergence, replacement or parallel comparison … Build labels, connectors and simple geometry natively … Do not ask the image model to rasterize the whole diagram or fabricate a dashboard. At final placement size verify the sequence and benefit are obvious.

Identify the alternatives, audience use case and one to three relevant criteria … the advertiser's comparison page is evidence of its positioning, not independent proof of every competitor limitation … A check mark, omission, crossed-out icon or unlabelled chart bar makes a factual claim. Where evidence disagrees, mark the criterion unresolved.
Write copy around the buyer's decision … Do not turn a capability difference into unsupported savings, quality rankings or a universal recommendation.
Inspect the company's comparison ads and linked comparison content … Derive a visual relationship from those references, not a compulsory versus table.
Three forms: One criterion, visible difference; Fit for the task; The decisive demonstration … Competitor ridicule, illegible caveats and fake zeroes weaken credibility.

Never generate comparison evidence, competitor UI or certification badges … Reduce the number of criteria or change the layout before reducing qualifiers to microtype. If removing a footnote changes who wins, the condition belongs in the main comparison.

Answer one real concern … from the brief, approved audience research or product context, not from inventing what a prospect fears … compatibility evidence answers only compatibility … If the evidence answers only part of the objection, narrow the wording; "contact sales" cannot stand in for an unsubstantiated reassuring headline.

Inspect the brand's actual concern-addressing ads … A reference's confident tone does not expand the evidence. Do not convert another brand's badge, certification or customer quote into a generic visual cue for trust.
"No risk," "zero effort" and "works with everything" require their own evidence … Use a question only when it genuinely helps frame the issue, keeping it neutral.
Three relationships: Answer first; Show the control; Concern and response. Not an obligatory shield icon or row of check marks. A lock illustration is atmosphere, not evidence.

Never generate certification seals, fake support messages or fabricated customer proof … Review as a skeptical buyer: does the evidence answer this exact concern, and does the destination continue that answer?

Separate opinion, observation, prediction and empirical fact in the copy … a factual industry assertion still needs an actual source with its date, population and scope. Do not turn a forecast into a settled result or a personal opinion into company policy.
Use the brand's original editorial ads to judge cadence, confidence, humor … preserve exact quotations and attribution … Do not invent a founder signature.

For a close companion, preserve the original ad's hierarchy, typographic character, image treatment, logo relationship and CTA treatment. Vary the actual argument or visual relationship intentionally. Do not remove observed texture or expressive imagery to default to a flat statement panel.
Three forms: A typographic thesis; An editorial image and argument; An explained distinction.

A portrait requires a real source … Graphs require supported data; a visual argument is not permission to invent category adoption curves … If no approved thesis can be recovered, derive only a supportable product position and record the missing editorial source.
Probe "Make an ad about our view of the industry" with an essay and without one.

Identify the exact idea … State what each important visual element stands for and which visible relationship makes the point … Record the relationship in preserve and review_needs before choosing or generating artwork … Check for unintended meanings.

Inspect the brand's relevant original ads before choosing a metaphor vocabulary. Their material, realism, humor, scale and visual tension reveal what fits this brand … Do not import rockets, glowing networks, puzzle pieces or growth arrows because the category is software.
Three approaches: A physical relationship; An unexpected juxtaposition; An editorial abstraction. Not a required three-option output.

Keep the chosen original's relevant composition or material treatment when the request asks for a close companion … the subject can change while edge softness, lighting and texture remain … In a new-concept request, make the semantic relationship distinct as well as changing its surface styling.
Generate the metaphorical component rather than the whole ad … Compare palette, light and material across the whole composition so separately generated assets support one visual argument.

Inspect the final image before reading the headline and name the relationship its arrangement conveys … If swapping in an unrelated headline leaves the image equally suitable … revise the arrangement.

Read the actual guide … A title alone can substantiate a guide's name, not its contents, findings, step count or completeness. Do not promise a downloadable resource unless the destination provides it … A statistic needs its actual population, period and source.

Use the brand's original editorial and promotional ads to judge density, tone and how much the artwork teaches … Preserve the selected original's information rhythm, artwork treatment, logo relationship and CTA treatment where continuity matters.
Three forms: One useful distinction; A brief field guide; A resource invitation. Not a preselected card grid.

For a resource invitation, compose the title and reason to read as one message group … A small topic illustration … does not automatically justify a large empty middle and a detached button … Use the shared component procedure to reflow the group together.
Probe "Make a useful ad from our guide" with a full guide and a title-only source.
